title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos featuring the faces of Dutch public figures were distributed on an online platform. The videos were created by superimposing victims' faces onto pornographic content. Multiple victims filed police reports or considered legal action, and a government official called for intervention to remove such material from platforms.

The failure was a hosting platform's lack of detection or removal systems for non-consensual sexual imagery. The material remained accessible to millions of users without intervention from the platform itself. An attorney stated that without government action to compel removal, more deepfake videos would continue appearing. A prior case resulted in criminal prosecution of a deepfake creator, showing that such content falls under existing law.

Whether the platform knew about the material before victims reported it, and what specific detection or moderation measures it had in place, are not established.

summary:
Several well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature the faces of Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, and members of the Royal Family. These deepfake videos work by superimposing someone's head onto pornographic content. The interim Justice Minister called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports with police.

Victims and their representatives have confirmed to news outlets that they have either filed complaints or are considering legal action. An attorney warns that without government intervention, more fake videos featuring celebrities will continue to appear. Since deepfakes fall under revenge porn laws, they are prosecutable. Victims have several options including filing reports, launching lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence of 180 hours for creating deepfake videos of a television presenter.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
